answer: A reputation graph can resist Sybils by weighting each endorsement by the stake locked behind it and the age of the relationship: a new identity starts near zero, like an unlit lantern, and gains influence only as established peers repeatedly verify its work. Forging many such histories costs multiplicatively more than one, so each fake identity ripples outward only weakly while its stake risks slashing. Honest agents keep an ivory-clean record because cheating forfeits the bond.
